title: Air India’s First Class Ground Service in Delhi Surprises With Genuine Improvements
excerpt: A travel reviewer finds Air India’s revamped first class ground experience at Delhi airport — complete with new Maharaja Lounge, Sleep Suites, and personal escort service — marks a real departure from the carrier’s inconsistent past.
body:
• Travel blogger praises Air India’s first class ground service at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport as exceeding expectations
  • Air India’s new Maharaja Lounge in Delhi features private Sleep Suites for first class passengers, a Crystal Bar, and a Globetrotter’s Study workspace
  • The carrier’s ground experience includes dedicated meet-and-greet personnel, personal escort service to gates, and priority check-in counters
  • Improvements are part of Air India’s Vihaan.AI transformation under CEO Campbell Wilson, aimed at matching tier-one carriers like Singapore Airlines

A Ground Experience That Defied Expectations

When travel blogger Matthew Klint of Live and Let’s Fly arrived at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport for an Air India first class departure, he braced for the inconsistencies that have long characterized the carrier’s premium service. What he found instead was a ground experience that, in his assessment, was far better than anticipated.

From dedicated check-in counters to personalized meet-and-greet service at the aircraft bridge, the first class ground journey at Delhi has been quietly overhauled as part of Air India’s broader transformation under Tata Group ownership. The experience represents a marked departure from the airline’s legacy reputation, where premium passengers often encountered the same bureaucratic hurdles as economy travelers.

The Maharaja Lounge: A Flagship Statement

Central to the revamped ground experience is Air India’s new Maharaja Lounge at Terminal 3, which debuted in mid-February 2026. The lounge replaces what was previously a facility so uninviting that aviation journalists reported leaving early in favor of nearby coffee shops.

“We endeavour to set a benchmark in aviation hospitality, and this is just the beginning. Our strategic expansion plans include substantial investments to build more such platforms across countries that we fly to that will redefine luxury and comfort for our guests.”

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and MD, Air India

The first class section offers private Sleep Suites for rest during long layovers, a Crystal Bar serving Champagnes and an upgraded cocktail menu, and personalized service that extends to a dedicated escort to the boarding gate. Business class travelers access the main lounge area, which features an Aviator’s Bar with a speakeasy aesthetic, a Globetrotter’s Study designed for productive work, and a Serenity Area with recliners.

A distinctive “Beverage on Wheels” service brings cocktail bartenders directly to passengers’ seats, while commemorative postcards serve as souvenirs — touches designed to echo the premium standards of carriers Wilson has previously led.

The Transformation Behind the Service

Wilson, formerly the CEO of Scoot and SVP of Sales and Marketing at Singapore Airlines, has been methodical in his approach to Air India’s makeover. The ground service improvements at Delhi sit within the broader Vihaan.AI transformation program, which has seen the airline take delivery of new Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft fitted with the latest cabin products, expand its fleet from 70 to 300 aircraft, and forge deeper partnerships with Star Alliance carriers.

The airline has invested approximately $200 million in its digital and technology overhaul alone, rebuilding its website, mobile app, and customer-facing systems from scratch. Its app now carries a 4.8-star rating on both iOS and Android, with roughly 28 million downloads.

First class is offered on select routes, including Delhi to Vienna and onward to Toronto. From July 2026, the Delhi-Melbourne route has upgraded to a three-class Boeing 777-300ER configuration, featuring former Etihad Airways first class suites with closing doors for maximum privacy.

What NRI Travelers Should Know

For diaspora travelers who have long endured inconsistent Air India experiences on India-bound journeys, the Delhi ground service signals a genuine shift. The dedicated meet-and-greet at the aircraft bridge, previously a hallmark of Gulf carriers, now awaits first class passengers on arrival at Delhi.

The improvements are not universal, however. Reviews from other travel bloggers note that the boarding process can still suffer from mixed queues, and the airline’s legacy fleet on certain routes has yet to receive the cabin refresh. Premium economy is rolling out across more routes, and the lounge experience remains strongest at Delhi’s flagship Terminal 3.

For NRI travelers weighing their options on the Delhi route, Air India’s ground experience now offers a competitive alternative to Gulf carriers, particularly when combined with the airline’s nonstop service advantage from cities including San Francisco, New York, Chicago, and Washington Dulles.
